title: BHOPAL
subtitle: The Night the City Woke
posterMeta: 2 DECEMBER 1984 - THE GAS - THE COUNT - THE CLAIMS
logline: A pesticide plant vented methyl isocyanate over Bhopal at midnight. The gas lasted one night; the argument over who counted has lasted four decades.

style.look: midnight sodium and cold cyan, wet concrete, oxidised steel, paper, dust in hard light, restrained typography
rules: Show the object before the explanation: a tank, a gauge, a ledger, a tap, a flame.
No bodies, no blood, no reconstruction of the dying. The aftermath carries the violence.
One idea per shot. The camera pushes, reveals or holds. It never drifts.
Cut on the voice. Do not park on a plate after the narration has stopped.
Every number on screen is an official figure or explicitly attributed.

sources.title: The Bhopal disaster and its aftermath: a review

blender.role: 3D sets, hero stills, camera moves, render passes, procedural tank farm, gauges, city rooftops and memorial

scenes.title: The city
scenes.purpose: Open on a sleeping city, then land the date and the title without a lecture.

narration.text: Bhopal, 2 December 1984.
A city sleeps beside a pesticide plant.

shots.camera: locked title card, grain and a slow push
shots.visual: The title arrives over a black field with a thin sodium line, holding just long enough to read.

transition.reason: One frame of sodium light opens the film; the title then holds in silence.

shots.camera: slow push over rooftops, lens 32
shots.visual: A dense roofscape at night: water tanks, antennas, a minaret, a few lit windows, and the plant's flare beyond.

transition.reason: The date lands on the city; a dissolve between a title and a place would soften the fact.

scenes.title: The plant
scenes.purpose: Establish the factory as a place of work and a place of storage, not a monster.

narration.text: The Union Carbide plant made pesticides for Indian farms.
Its tanks held methyl isocyanate, a chemical that attacks the lungs.
Tank 610 held about forty-two tonnes of it.
The safety systems were not all working.

shots.camera: wide, low, the gate and the sign
shots.visual: The plant gate at night under a sodium lamp, a bicycle at the fence, the factory wall and stacks behind.

transition.reason: The title gives way to the plant gate whole; the place arrives without a reveal.

shots.camera: wide from the pipe rack, lens 30
shots.visual: Four storage tanks and a flare tower under a low sky, pipework crossing the foreground.

transition.reason: The gate opens onto the tank farm; the scale jumps on a hard cut.

shots.camera: slow push, the sign filling the frame
shots.visual: A weathered company sign bolted to concrete: UNION CARBIDE / INDIA LIMITED / BHOPAL PESTICIDES PLANT.

transition.reason: The company name arrives as a statement after the tanks, not as a decorative wipe.

shots.camera: low tracking line down the pipe rack
shots.visual: A corridor of pipes, catwalk and steam, receding into sodium light.

transition.reason: The pipe corridor continues the plant interior; the cut keeps the factory one system.

shots.camera: upward tilt, the flare against the sky
shots.visual: The flare stack burns above the tank farm, a thin orange line in the dark.

transition.reason: The flare lands with forty-two tonnes; the number is the cut.

scenes.title: The warning
scenes.purpose: Make the failure mechanical and legible: water, pressure, a shut refrigeration unit, an offline flare.

narration.text: The official inquiry found water had entered Tank 610.
Pressure and temperature climbed.
The refrigeration unit had been shut down.
The flare tower was offline, and the scrubber could not cope.
No public warning prepared the city.

shots.camera: low three-quarter on the handwheel
shots.visual: A corroded handwheel and a tagged valve, lit by one work lamp, pipework running into the dark.

transition.reason: The flare ring becomes the handwheel rim; the same circle now controls the flow.

shots.camera: macro, the needle in the red
shots.visual: A pressure gauge fills the frame, its needle deep in the red arc, condensation on the glass.

transition.reason: The handwheel gives way to the gauge that measures what the valve let in.

shots.camera: close on the wall clock, hands at 00:45
shots.visual: A wall clock reads 00:45 above a logbook; the minute hand is the only moving thing in the room.

transition.reason: The gauge needle and the clock minute hand read the same angle; the cut lands on the tick.

shots.camera: hold on the cold flare tower
shots.visual: The flare tower stands unlit against the sky, its tip dark; the tank farm below is a row of shadows.

transition.reason: The clock time gives way to the unlit flare; the failure is now a fact.

shots.camera: slow push across the analog panel
shots.visual: A wall of dials, switches and one red warning lamp; an empty chair and a logbook.

transition.reason: The empty panel holds the last line; no warning came from it.

scenes.title: The release
scenes.purpose: Move the gas through the city without reconstructing death; the sound carries the scale.

narration.text: Around midnight, the tank vented.
A cloud of MIC rolled low over the railway colony and the old city.
People woke with burning eyes and no breath.
They ran into the dark, away from a smell they could not name.
The gas moved through the streets before the city understood.

shots.camera: low angle, the tower and a plume of vapor
shots.visual: Vapor spills from the tank farm and crosses the flare tower; the flare is still dark.

transition.reason: Vapour crosses the frame; the dissolve is the gas, not a scene change.

shots.camera: tracking at ground level, vapor in the light
shots.visual: A low corridor of pipes and steam, the light scattering in a pale cloud.

transition.reason: The haze continues through the pipe corridor; same gas, same low light.

shots.camera: low, the lamp above an empty lane
shots.visual: A narrow street under one sodium lamp; shutters closed, a bicycle, a bucket, a puddle holding the light.

transition.reason: The gas reaches the street; cut to the lamp before the dissolve can become a habit.

shots.camera: high wide, the roofscape under a pale cloud
shots.visual: The city from above, a low haze moving between roofs, windows lighting one by one.

transition.reason: The roofscape shows the scale; a hard cut keeps the city from becoming wallpaper.

shots.camera: low, the siren horn against the sky
shots.visual: A rooftop siren, horn pointed at the city, moon behind it; the pole and braces read as a skeleton.

transition.reason: The city alarm turns the frame; the siren is already in the air before the horn arrives.

scenes.title: The count
scenes.purpose: Put the numbers on screen with their sources and their disagreements intact.

narration.text: The official immediate death toll was 2,259.
Madhya Pradesh later confirmed 3,787 deaths.
Survivors' clinics estimate 8,000 died in the first weeks, and 8,000 more since.
More than 500,000 people were exposed.

shots.camera: overhead, the front page fills the frame
shots.visual: A newspaper desk under a brass lamp: the word BHOPAL, a typewriter, a telephone, a cup, a cigarette.

transition.reason: 2,259 lands on the last syllable; no fade, no flash, no cushion.

shots.camera: push between shelves to the reading table
shots.visual: Archive shelves and boxes; one open file on a table under a green lamp.

transition.reason: 3,787 lands like a stamp on the file.

shots.camera: three-quarter on the window and oxygen cylinder
shots.visual: A clinic room lit by a moonlit window and one bulb: an oxygen cylinder, a chair, a bottle, a curtain.

transition.reason: 8,000 lands with the clinic's count; the hard cut refuses consolation.

shots.camera: low, the wall of plaques and marigolds
shots.visual: A stone memorial wall with brass plaques, marigolds and candles; the names are abstract, not invented.

transition.reason: The clinic gives way to the memorial wall; the exposed count is the bridge.

scenes.title: The settlement
scenes.purpose: Follow the claim from the courtroom to the ledger, and show what a settlement does not settle.

narration.text: In 1989, the Supreme Court approved a $470 million settlement.
The claims were consolidated under the Indian government.
Union Carbide's chairman was charged in India, but never extradited.
In 2010, seven former employees were convicted. The sentence was two years.
The settlement did not end the argument.

shots.camera: overhead, the amount is the subject
shots.visual: An open ledger under a lamp: SETTLEMENT, $470,000,000, 1989, a stamp, a pen, a gavel.

transition.reason: The ledger edge wipes the frame; the settlement arrives as paper.

shots.camera: wide from the aisle, the empty bench
shots.visual: A wooden courtroom, empty: the bench, the witness box, the clerk's table, the scales, the fan.

transition.reason: The stamp's circular seal opens onto the courtroom scales; the law takes over the page.

shots.camera: slow push along the files
shots.visual: Archive boxes and files, the paper trail of a case that outlived the hearing.

transition.reason: The courtroom gives way to the archive; the case outlives the hearing.

shots.camera: close on the headline and the date
shots.visual: The newspaper again, the date 1984 beside a stack of later clippings.

transition.reason: The newspaper edge wipes the frame; the headline is the next document.

shots.camera: low from the clerk's table, the bench in shadow
shots.visual: The courtroom from the clerk's table: an empty bench, the scales, the fan turning above the room.

transition.reason: The conviction lands on a hard cut; two years is not a transition.

shots.camera: hold, the sign in the sodium light
shots.visual: The company sign again, rust running from its bolts; the name is the same, the ownership is not.

transition.reason: The sign returns without a flourish; the name is still there.

scenes.title: The water
scenes.purpose: Bring the disaster into the present through the tap, the sample and the body.

narration.text: The plant stopped production in 1986.
Its waste and contaminated water remained.
Survivors still carry the exposure in their bodies.
Groundwater near the site is still contaminated.

shots.camera: hold at the end of the corridor
shots.visual: The corridor recedes into fluorescent light; the stretcher is still empty.

transition.reason: The corridor is empty; the cut refuses to fill it.

shots.camera: macro, the jar and its label
shots.visual: A glass jar of murky water on a lab bench, labelled BHOPAL / WATER SAMPLE, with a vial and a pipette.

transition.reason: The jar is the next object in the chain: water, sample, body.

shots.camera: slow push, the empty chair
shots.visual: The clinic room again; the oxygen cylinder and the empty chair hold the frame.

transition.reason: The clinic holds the exposure; no effect is needed.

shots.camera: low, the tap and the bucket
shots.visual: A corroded standpipe and tap above a bucket, a toxic-looking puddle, barrels and a warning sign.

transition.reason: The tap is the last object before the flame; the drip is the bridge.

scenes.title: The memory
scenes.purpose: Move from the archive to the memorial without turning the dead into decoration.

narration.text: Every year, Bhopal remembers.
The disaster helped push India's Environment Protection Act in 1986.
It did not settle the question of who was responsible.
The memorial is a wall, a flame, and an unfinished argument.

shots.camera: macro, the flame inside the glass ring
shots.visual: A single flame in a brass bowl behind glass, petals on the stone, the background almost black.

transition.reason: The tap drip and the memorial flame share a vertical shape and screen position; the drip sound carries into the flame.

shots.camera: low, the plaques and the word BHOPAL
shots.visual: The memorial wall: brass plaques, marigolds, candles, the word BHOPAL and the year 1984.

transition.reason: The flame gives way to the wall; memory is a place, not a glow.

shots.camera: wide, the city and the plant beyond
shots.visual: The roofscape again, the plant's flare still on the horizon; the city is awake.

transition.reason: The city returns; the plant is still on the horizon.

shots.camera: pull back from the open file
shots.visual: The archive file open under the lamp; boxes recede into the dark.

transition.reason: The record closes the scene; the argument stays open.

scenes.title: The claims
scenes.purpose: Close on a sentence, not a spectacle.

narration.text: The gas lasted one night.
The claims have lasted four decades.

shots.camera: hold, the flame in the dark
shots.visual: The memorial flame, the only warm light in the frame.

transition.reason: The last scene returns to the flame without an effect.

shots.camera: locked, the title returns as an end card
shots.visual: The title card returns over black with the date and a single line of source text.
shots.text: THE CLAIMS HAVE LASTED FOUR DECADES

transition.reason: The film closes to black; the only dip is the end.

signature: needle match: gauge needle to clock hand
valve iris: handwheel rim to flare ring to court seal
water/flame match: tap drip to memorial flame
gas haze: dissolve only where gas is the subject
siren whip: horn to street lamp with a pre-lapped siren
paper edge: ledger and newspaper wipe the frame
